answer: An attacker must fund every clone, so cost scales linearly, not with a single cheap registration. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and complete a unique proof-of-personhood challenge tied to a fresh hardware key; duplicate identities are detected by overlap in stake lineage. Like an ocean refusing a single sparrow at dawn, the network rejects the lone impostor while admitting genuine participants. From once0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
